note: Research notes from outside the laboratory. Each says how it is known. None of these is a discovery: only experiments (knowledge.json) can make one. labStatus says what the laboratory has done with it.

grades.source: the code was cloned or fetched and read
grades.third-party: a write-up by someone else; not checked against the tool
grades.search-snippet: only a search-result summary was available
grades.unreachable: the host could not be reached from the research environment

sources.title: LuaXen (ByteXenon)
claims: MIT licence; a single commit, dated 2024-09-29 in the clone; 174 files.
A toolkit in pure Lua: lexer, parser, compiler, decompiler, minifier, interpreter, assembler, packer.
Its obfuscator example runs two stages in order: Obfuscator.IronBrikked.ObfuscateScript, then Obfuscator.ASTObfuscator.ObfuscateScript on the result: a nested, multi-stage case.
sources.labReason: Needs a real Lua runtime (package.path, debug.getinfo, require of its own modules). None is available in the research environment, so no sample output was produced and no compatibility claim exists.

sources.title: Luraph (lura.ph)
claims: The vendor site (lura.ph) could not be reached from the research environment (the egress proxy refuses the host), so its documentation pages were not read; an attempt to add the host to the environment was declined.

The vendor's own GitHub organisation could be read. Its macro SDK repository (https://github.com/Luraph/macrosdk) states that it holds stubs for all Luraph macros, and its commit history dates the SDK updates for v14 (2024-04-23), v15 (2026-08-10) and v15.1 (2026-10-03): see histories/luraph-macrosdk.json.
A web search found no official changelog. Third-party pages label obfuscated files v13.6.x, v14.3 and v14.4.1.
sources.labReason: Version identification from a banner and from the macro set of an unprotected script is implemented and tested against the vendor's data. No output of any Luraph version has been obtained from a source the lab may use, so reconstruction has never been tried and nothing is claimed for it.

sources.title: Prometheus documentation and issue tracker
claims: Upstream documentation has moved to prometheus-lua.github.io/Prometheus/docs; the GitBook copy labels itself a legacy mirror.
The issue tracker lists Vmify bugs, among them one where Vmify applied to the AntiTamper step's code can produce failing code (issue 155, reported Nov 2023).
sources.labReason: Prometheus is measured with real tool output in data/compat.json (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md), not by this laboratory.

sources.title: Hercules (zeusssz)
claims: Its README says the VirtualMachine and bytecode_encoding modules are disabled automatically for Luau output.
sources.labReason: Measured with real tool output in data/compat.json.

sources.title: Baza Obfuscator; EVIL AXE Studios
claims: Baza Obfuscator is advertised as a Discord bot with a ChaCha20-encrypted VM; its code is not published.
EVIL AXE Studios is described as a wrapper around Prometheus.
sources.labReason: No code and no sample output.

sources.title: ByteLuaObfuscator (kosuke14)
claims: A search listing describes a bytecode-method obfuscator without Luau support. A clone attempt was refused (the repository asked for credentials), so its code was not read.

sources.title: Luraph v14 documentation (lura.ph/dashboard/documents/v14)
claims: Per a search-result summary of the vendor's page: VM Compression returned in v14; four new settings (Optimization Level, Enable FFI Library, Hardcode Globals, Static Environment); an enforceSettings option for POST /obfuscate/new and multipart/form-data payloads; and a note that Luraph v15 has been released.
sources.labReason: The page could not be fetched, so these statements come from a summary of it, not from the page. Not used to claim anything beyond what the summary says.

sources.title: Luraph/macrosdk: the vendor's SDK repository and its history
claims: README: 'Macro SDK with function stubs for all Luraph macros'; it says to update the file 'when newer versions of Luraph are released' and points to the official macros documentation for the complete reference.

Commits (read from a clone, text only): 2024-02-02 initial upload; 2024-04-23 'update sdk for luraph v14'; 2026-08-10 'update sdk for luraph v15'; 2026-10-03 'update sdk for luraph v15.1'; 2026-10-06 adds an UNSAFE_ENVIRONMENT attribute.

Macro sets by generation, derived from the file at each commit: 7, 11, 12 and 14 macros. The v15 update removes ENCFUNC, FUNCENC, JIT, JIT_MAX, NO_UPVALUES and NO_VIRTUALIZE and adds ATTRIBUTES, BUFENC/ENCBUF, OBFUSCATED, PRECHECK, REWRITE and STACKALLOC; v15.1 adds ASSUME and OPAQUE.
sources.labReason: This is the evidence behind the version-aware identification of Luraph macros (capability luraph.macro-generation). It describes the SDK stubs, not the protected output.

sources.title: Third-party 'Luraph deobfuscator' repositories (four READMEs read as text)
claims: Four repositories claim to deobfuscate Luraph (targets: v11.5/v11.8.1 in one, v14.x experimental and v15 in two, v15.1 in one). One README says of itself 'This deobf is shit do not use it' and credits an AI model; one states it provides no Luraph support. Two mention macros (LPH_ENCFUNC, LPH_NO_VIRTUALIZE) that the vendor's SDK dropped at v15.
None of their claims were tested, and none of their code was run: repositories like these are a common way to distribute malware. They are recorded as claims of low credibility.
sources.labReason: Read as text only, by policy.

sources.title: Copies of Luraph-protected scripts on document-sharing sites
claims: Search summaries say copies of scripts carry banners naming Luraph v14.3 and v13.6.x. Nothing else was taken from them.
sources.labReason: Other people's protected scripts, without their originals: there is nothing to compare a reconstruction with and no basis to use them as test cases, so they were not collected.

sources.title: Small VM and obfuscator repositories found by search (encrypted-luau-vm, a Luarmor listing)
claims: Their READMEs were read; the extractor found no technical statements in them (versions, features, macros). Two further repositories (LennyObf, ByteLuaObfuscator) could not be read.
sources.labReason: No output samples and no technical description: nothing to measure.
